title: Nested localising tensor ideals give isomorphic weak rings of the associated pure-injectives
author: Paul Balmer
work: Homological support of big objects in tensor-triangulated categories
source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 7 (2020), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.135
difficulty_reason: The proposition is about a proper localising tensor ideal cC containing a localising tensor ideal cB, and claims that the weak rings EB and EC attached to the two ideals are isomorphic in the ambient category in a way compatible with their unit maps (statement lines 505-508). The proof factors the Gabriel quotient into two steps and computes the intermediate object tilde E as the image of EC in the intermediate quotient, then runs an injective-hull argument: the unit is a monomorphism by a cited criterion, the injective hull of the unit in the intermediate category maps into tilde E by a split monomorphism, and exactness of the intermediate localisation together with full faithfulness of its right adjoint forces the complementary summand to vanish (proof lines 511-533). The step that carries the content is that vanishing argument, since it is what converts a split monomorphism into an isomorphism; the descent to the ambient category is then a cited clause. H2.
